differences.title: 1. CONSENSUS MODEL
differences.leftDesc: CockroachDB stores data in replicated key ranges, each managed by a Raft group with leaders and followers. Linearizable reads can be served by coordinating leases and Raft state without a separate metadata service.
differences.rightDesc: YugabyteDB also uses Raft per data range, but its architecture centers around a PostgreSQL-compatible layer coordinating with tablet/range leaders. Leader changes and quorum reads are handled similarly, with different internal control paths.

differences.title: 2. TRANSACTION LIFECYCLE
differences.leftDesc: CockroachDB implements distributed transactions using serializable isolation with timestamp ordering and transaction records, coordinating via its distributed SQL layer. It optimizes commit paths using batch requests and parallel range access.
differences.rightDesc: YugabyteDB provides distributed transactions with PostgreSQL semantics while coordinating across nodes using its own transaction machinery (tablet leader routing, two-phase commit-like flows, and intent/timestamp management). Performance hinges on conflict handling strategies.

differences.title: 3. QUERY PLANNING & EXECUTION
differences.leftDesc: CockroachDB’s distributed SQL planner decomposes queries into physical operators aligned to key ranges and distributes execution to nodes holding required ranges. It uses statistics, join ordering, and partition-aware execution primitives.
differences.rightDesc: YugabyteDB’s YSQL uses PostgreSQL-derived optimizer behavior, augmented to account for distributed execution with tablets/partitions. Query plans are adapted into distributed tasks with leader-aware routing and parallel scan/aggregate patterns.

differences.title: 4. STORAGE LAYOUT & UPDATES
differences.leftDesc: CockroachDB uses MVCC over an LSM storage engine, writing intents and versions into RocksDB-like structures. Background compaction and range rebalancing manage garbage collection and maintain read performance under heavy writes.
differences.rightDesc: YugabyteDB uses MVCC with LSM storage and organizes data into tablets (ranges) that replicate via Raft. Its update and compaction behavior is tuned for distributed workloads, with differences in how intents and version cleanup are scheduled.

differences.title: 5. SCHEMA & TOPOLOGY MANAGEMENT
differences.leftDesc: CockroachDB’s metadata and range placement are handled by its internal control plane that continuously rebalances replicas. It tracks liveness, constraints, and zone configurations to move data while maintaining availability.
differences.rightDesc: YugabyteDB uses a master/coordinator approach for cluster metadata and tablet assignment, then relies on tablet leaders for serving. It supports zone/region placement, balancing, and schema distribution through different control-plane components.

differences.title: 6. READ CONSISTENCY OPTIONS
differences.leftDesc: CockroachDB supports multiple read modes, including strongly consistent and follower-allowed reads with bounded staleness. Under the hood it leverages read timestamps and leaseholder behavior to avoid violating isolation.
differences.rightDesc: YugabyteDB provides read consistency controls for strongly consistent and potentially stale reads, including follower/replica servicing patterns. The system uses leader/follower state and quorum rules to ensure user-selected consistency levels are respected.

differences.title: 7. OPERATIONS & ECOSYSTEM INTEGRATION
differences.leftDesc: CockroachDB emphasizes a Go-based distributed SQL engine with tooling like cockroach cli, built-in changefeeds, and schema management patterns tailored to its architecture. Its monitoring integrates with built-in metrics and standard observability stacks.
differences.rightDesc: YugabyteDB integrates tightly with the PostgreSQL ecosystem via YSQL: drivers, ORMs, and extensions. Ops center UI/CLI and observability hooks map cluster topology and tablet health into Postgres-oriented workflows.
